The starting compound has molecular formula C8H9NO and 1H-NMR data:
- 9.72 ppm (t, 1H): aldehyde proton coupled to a CH2 group.
- 3.66 ppm (d, 2H): CH2 group adjacent to the aldehyde.
- 6.98 ppm (d, 2H) and 6.51 ppm (d, 2H): para-substituted aromatic ring with electron-withdrawing (CH2CHO) and electron-donating (NH2) groups.
- 6.27 ppm (bs, 2H): NH2 protons.
This identifies the compound as 4-aminophenylacetaldehyde.

Reaction sequence:
1. NaNO2 + HCl: Diazotization of the aromatic amine to form a diazonium salt.
2. H2O: Hydrolysis of the diazonium salt to a phenol, yielding 4-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde.
3. aq. KOH, Heat: Aldol condensation. Two molecules of 4-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde undergo base-catalyzed self-condensation. The enolate of one molecule attacks the carbonyl of another, forming an aldol intermediate (3-hydroxy-2,4-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)butanal). Under heat, dehydration occurs to give the conjugated α,β-unsaturated aldehyde, 2,4-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)but-2-enal.

This matches option (A).

Answer: A
